reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource-level rubric, fresh-review framework, VisionPrescription context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate prepass, local R4/R6 VisionPrescription StructureDefinitions, and behavior reports as needed. I independently checked the R4/R6 local differential element lists and found no direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding whose `affectedResources` include `VisionPrescription`. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 VisionPrescription was trial-use/FMM 2, so it carries neutral stability pressure rather than a strong normative preservation burden. That lets the actual mechanism dominate: optional R6 additions are acceptable when they preserve R4-to-R6 instance validity, while safety or business loss during R6-to-R4 conversion still deserves explicit guidance.

overall.oneLineConclusion: VisionPrescription keeps its identity and R4-valid local content remains structurally representable in R6; the material work is preserving optional R6 request linkage and priority during down-conversion, not a resource-level migration program.

reasoning.thesisMd: VisionPrescription is not removed, renamed, split, or substantively remodeled. The canonical identity, DomainResource base, required R4 fields, lens specification backbone, shared cardinalities, shared types, reference targets, modifier behavior, and existing required code sets are stable. The only local structural findings are optional R6 additions: `basedOn`, `groupIdentifier`, and `priority`.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is low-material-change for R4-to-R6. Existing R4 instances do not need a resource-wide transform to satisfy the R6 local content model because no R4 local element was removed, renamed, narrowed, or made stricter. R6-to-R4 exchange is less trivial: populated `basedOn` or `groupIdentifier` can carry request provenance/grouping that R4 has no native slot for, and populated `priority` can carry urgency that should not be silently dropped.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A resource-level migration program is not already unavoidable. The reviewed changes also do not present an avoidable base R4-to-R6 break: they are optional additions rather than replaced or tightened R4 fields. That supports `no-special-break-avoidance-needed` for the current resource-level conclusion, while still requiring normal per-change scrutiny if future R6 edits introduce removals, renames, mandatory fields, or narrowed bindings.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: No low-cost less-breaking base R6 design is apparent for these specific additions. Adding first-class optional request-pattern fields is already the compatibility-preserving base approach for R4-to-R6. For `priority`, an extension-only design would reduce older-schema rejection but would undercut the R6 goal of a standard urgency signal; the right mitigation is cross-version extension or conversion guidance for R6-to-R4, not removing the optional base element.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP REST behavior finding was assigned to VisionPrescription, and a direct scan of the supplied behavior reports found no `affectedResources` match. The shared Resource/DomainResource operation, search, and HTTP findings can affect generic clients operating on any resource, but they are not VisionPrescription-specific migration pressure and should not change this resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No`, migration shape `low-material-change`, and compatibility leverage `no-special-break-avoidance-needed`. I agree after checking the underlying structure report and definitions. The nuance I would preserve is that `priority` is still a safety/business-relevant down-conversion concern even though it is not a reason to revisit the base R6 resource design.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition shape. Remaining uncertainty comes from the absence of an official R4-to-R6 VisionPrescription narrative diff, missing formal ValueSet expansions in the local package material, no production usage data for the new fields, and the fact that the reviewed R6 input is ballot4 rather than a final release.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds request priority with required priority codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most material local finding and the best stress test for the resource conclusion. It is safety/business relevant because dropping `urgent`, `asap`, or `stat` during R6-to-R4 conversion can change fulfillment priority, especially because R6 says missing priority means normal priority. It still does not make a resource-level R4-to-R6 migration unavoidable: `priority` is optional, no R4 field was replaced, and the required binding applies only when the new R6 element is populated.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds request linkage and grouping elements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `basedOn` and `groupIdentifier` matter for order reconciliation, audit, and grouped fulfillment when R6 data is downgraded or exchanged with R4 systems. They are nevertheless local optional additions that preserve R4-to-R6 validity and align with request-pattern metadata; avoiding them or making them extension-only would lose first-class lineage/grouping support rather than prevent an R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource operation change can affect generic clients or servers that expose metadata operations on VisionPrescription instances, but it is not a VisionPrescription-specific behavior finding. It should be handled in the Resource/API review and not counted as evidence that VisionPrescription itself needs a resource-level migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search-parameter metadata change may affect generated clients and conformance tooling across many resources. It is relevant background for generic VisionPrescription search clients, but the supplied context has no direct VisionPrescription search behavior finding and the shared issue should not drive the resource-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm cross-version guidance for `VisionPrescription.priority`: R6-to-R4 converters should preserve `urgent`, `asap`, and `stat` in an official cross-version extension, local extension, related order artifact, or explicit manual-review queue rather than silently dropping them into normal-priority semantics.

Document R6-to-R4 handling for `basedOn` and `groupIdentifier`, including tests with multiple `basedOn` references and a populated group identifier so request provenance and grouping are not accidentally lost.
Keep shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search compatibility work separate from the VisionPrescription resource conclusion so base API breaks are not double-counted across resources.

caveats: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was assigned specifically to VisionPrescription.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may still affect generic clients operating on VisionPrescription, but they were treated as context only as required.
No official R4-to-R6 VisionPrescription diff narrative or production usage corpus was available in the supplied local inputs.
The local ValueSet resources did not include formal expansions, and the reviewed R6 package is 6.0.0-ballot4 rather than a final R6 release.
